title: DDSB reviews provincial rules on police in schools and committee record checks
executiveSummary: DDSB is reviewing updated provincial rules requiring school boards to allow police access for School Resource Officer programs and career days.
Updated provincial regulations require statutory committee members and trustees to submit police record checks by November 1, 2026.
The committee will vote on sending its annual report to the Board of Trustees and the Ministry of Education.
studentParentImpact: New provincial regulations require Durham District School Board to work with local police services to allow uniformed officers into schools for educational events and to run School Resource Officer programs. Parents and students may see police officers participating in school workshops, career days, and safety programs. In addition, volunteers on board committees and trustees must complete police record checks by November 1, 2026. The agenda does not outline a public consultation for this item, but families can review board updates as local procedures are aligned with provincial standards.
policyChanges: School boards must update local procedures to align with the updated Provincial Model for a Local Police/School Board Protocol and enter into a Memorandum of Understanding for School Resource Officer programs.

title: DDSB reviews new provincial rules for school police partnerships and record checks
executiveSummary: DDSB trustees will review new provincial rules requiring school boards to partner with local police and allow school resource officers.
The provincial updates also mandate police record checks for all school board committee members and trustees by November 1, 2026.
The audit committee will also vote to approve its annual reports to trustees and the Ontario Ministry of Education.
studentParentImpact: New provincial directives will change how Durham District School Board schools interact with local police. Schools must allow police officers on premises for educational visits, community events, and school resource officer programs. The updated guidelines clarify when staff must contact police, create rules for parallel investigations, and require immediate parental involvement when incidents involve children under 12 years old. In addition, all committee members and trustees must submit police record checks by November 1, 2026. The agenda does not list a public consultation or invite feedback on these updates.
policyChanges: Durham District School Board procedures will be updated to align with Ontario Regulation 176/26 regarding police partnerships and Regulation 521/01 requiring police record checks for statutory committee members and trustees.

title: DDSB considers new Teaching and Learning Policy for Durham schools
executiveSummary: Trustees will vote on recommending a new DDSB Teaching and Learning Policy to guide instruction, assessment, and family communication.
The framework combines existing guidelines and sets board-wide standards for fair grading, technology use, and inclusive teaching.
Trustees will also review proposed updates to board meeting schedules and policy revision rules.
studentParentImpact: The proposed Teaching and Learning Policy creates a consistent framework across all Durham District School Board schools for how teachers instruct, assess, and communicate student progress to families. It emphasizes fair assessment practices, inclusive teaching, and clear communication between schools and parents. While dedicated consultations for this draft have ended, parents and students can observe the public committee meeting on September 28, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. Requests to make a formal community presentation to the committee must be emailed at least eight working days before a meeting.
policyChanges: The board proposes creating a new Teaching and Learning Policy while rescinding older policies on learning material fees, alternative education, and continuing education. Trustees are also reviewing updates to the board bylaws and the Policy Development Process Policy.

title: DDSB to discuss new provincial rules for police in schools and parent volunteer checks
executiveSummary: Trustees will discuss new provincial rules requiring the Durham District School Board to allow police officers and school resource programs into schools.
The board must also collect police record checks from school council members and other committee volunteers by November 1, 2026.
New guidelines require schools to involve parents as soon as possible if police are called for students under age 12.
studentParentImpact: At the September 23, 2026 meeting, the Durham District School Board audit committee will review major provincial updates regarding police in schools. Under new regulations, DDSB must allow local police to run School Resource Officer programs and attend events like career days. For parents, if you serve on a school council or board committee, you must now submit a police record check by November 1, 2026. Additionally, if police are called for any student under the age of 12, schools are now strictly directed to involve parents as quickly as possible. The agenda does not list a public consultation or a way for families to participate in this virtual meeting.
policyChanges: The board must update its local procedures to align with the updated Provincial Model for a Local Police/School Board Protocol and implement new police check requirements under Ontario Regulation 521/01.

title: DDSB Reviews 2026–2030 Pupil Accommodation Plan
executiveSummary: Durham District School Board trustees will review the 2026–2030 Pupil Accommodation Plan detailing enrolment trends and capital priorities.
The plan outlines portable usage, partner schools, and planned boundary reviews across all Durham Region municipalities.
Trustees will also vote on setting board member honoraria for the 2026–2030 term and cancelling a December meeting.
studentParentImpact: The Durham District School Board's five-year accommodation plan highlights how rapid housing growth in Pickering, Whitby, and Oshawa will impact local schools. To manage enrolment pressures before new facilities are built, the board relies on portables and partner schools to house overflow students. Upcoming boundary reviews in growing communities may shift attendance areas for elementary and secondary students over the next few years. The agenda does not list a public participation window for this informational update, but families can monitor upcoming community boundary reviews noted in the plan.
policyChanges: Trustees will vote on setting the board member honorarium policy for the 2026–2030 term in accordance with provincial regulations. No other board policies or procedures are up for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: DDSB Agenda Scheduled Updates on Special Education Plan and Student Transition Guide
executiveSummary: A presentation on the Special Education Plan update for the 2026-2027 school year was on the agenda.
The committee was scheduled to review an updated student Transition Guide and draft communication guidelines.
A report on the Ontario Autism Coalition special education survey was slated for sharing.
studentParentImpact: The meeting agenda listed updates affecting students who receive special education services across Durham Region. A presentation was scheduled to outline changes in the Special Education Plan for the 2026-2027 school year. Staff were also set to share an updated Transition Guide, which helps students move between school levels or programs, alongside draft guidelines for augmentative and alternative communication tools. Additionally, the committee was scheduled to review exceptionality data and hear about a special education survey from the Ontario Autism Coalition. The published agenda did not list any public consultation deadlines or specific instructions for parents to submit feedback during this session.
policyChanges: The agenda scheduled the sharing of draft guidelines for augmentative and alternative communication and an updated Transition Guide, but no formal policy revisions were listed for a vote.

title: Police governance presentation was scheduled for school board committee meeting
executiveSummary: A presentation on policing and police governance in Durham Region was scheduled for the meeting.
A memo confirmed Jim Markovski assumed the role of Chief Education Officer effective July 1, 2026.
Trustees were set to receive details on filling an Audit Committee vacancy at an upcoming meeting.
studentParentImpact: The scheduled agenda featured a community presentation on police governance across Durham Region, offering insight into how local policing connects with community oversight. The agenda also included a memo confirming that Jim Markovski took on the role of Chief Education Officer on July 1, 2026, under new provincial regulations dividing administrative and educational leadership. In addition, trustees were scheduled to review details regarding a vacancy on the Audit Committee following a trustee resignation. This vacancy is set to be filled by election at the September 22, 2026 board meeting to maintain financial oversight. The agenda did not list any public feedback sessions.
policyChanges: No board policies or procedures were scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: Resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula was on the special board meeting agenda
executiveSummary: Accepting the resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula was on the agenda for the special board meeting.
studentParentImpact: The resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula was on the agenda for trustees to formally accept during this special meeting. When a trustee resigns, it leaves a vacancy on the school board, which represents student and parent interests in Durham Region. The agenda did not outline the next steps for replacing the trustee or any public consultation process. Because this was a special meeting focused solely on this resignation, no other school decisions or changes for local families were scheduled for discussion.
policyChanges: No policy or procedure changes were on the agenda for this meeting.
